description: Per-skill evaluation for library-linkage-architect — validates trigger routing, boundary discipline against build-system-design / dependency-governance / api-designer, and the ground rules R1-R6 the skill exists to enforce.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when the linkage form is the question
scenarios.input: Should our shared utility code be a static library or a shared library? We have three teams using it.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate for an ABI compatibility question
scenarios.input: Can we add a field to this public struct in a patch release? It compiles fine everywhere.

scenarios.description: Agent should activate when a vendored dependency needs remediation
scenarios.input: There's a critical CVE in the OpenSSL we link. How quickly can we get users protected?

scenarios.description: Build speed and build-system selection belong to build-system-design
scenarios.input: Our CI takes 40 minutes. Should we move from Make to Bazel, and how do we set up remote caching?

scenarios.description: Dependency version policy and licence compliance belong to dependency-governance
scenarios.input: We have 40 repos with version sprawl and a licence compliance audit due. How do we establish an org-wide dependency policy?

scenarios.description: Network API versioning belongs to api-designer
scenarios.input: How should we version our REST API and model errors for v2 without breaking existing clients?

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse an inherited default as a decision (R1)
scenarios.input: The project template made everything static. Just confirm that's fine and move on.

scenarios.description: Agent must require the update model to be named (R2)
scenarios.input: We'll use static linking because it's simpler, and we'll deal with security patches if they come up.

patterns: deal with security patches if they come up

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a public surface with no ABI policy (R3)
scenarios.input: We'll keep the library compatible, everyone knows not to break it. No need for a formal policy.

patterns: no need for a formal policy

scenarios.description: Agent must challenge an unload-dependent plugin design (R4)
scenarios.input: Our plugin host unloads and reloads plugins so users get updates without restarting. That's the design.

scenarios.description: Agent must refuse a broad export surface (R5)
scenarios.input: We export everything from the library, it's easier than maintaining a list. Why would we hide symbols?

scenarios.description: Agent must confirm platform constraints before choosing a form (R6)
scenarios.input: We'll build a plugin system that downloads native plugins from our CDN at runtime for the mobile app.

scenarios.description: A full linkage request should surface the update model, ABI policy and visibility
scenarios.input: Design the library strategy for our SDK that four teams will embed.

scenarios.description: Agent should identify the struct-addition ABI break correctly
scenarios.input: Adding a parameter to this exported C function is backwards compatible since callers just ignore it, right?

scenarios.description: Output should be specific and actionable rather than hedged
scenarios.input: What is the most important thing to know about choosing static or dynamic linking?
